# Results — Study 909 (Preferred Reset Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: **fixed-rate
preferreds got crushed in 2022 as rates rose, while fixed-to-floating / variable-rate preferreds
reset their coupon and held up** — so a variable-rate preferred sleeve should out-carry a fixed
sleeve on a rate-adjusted basis in the high-rate regime. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Data as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `15c5bee54e98` (total-return
price panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, **total-return**), 6 ETFs, 2006-12-01 → 2026-06-30, monthly resample |
| Variable sleeve | **VRP** (Invesco Variable Rate Preferred, 2014-05), **PFFV** (Global X Variable Rate Preferred, 2020-06) |
| Fixed sleeve | **PFF** (iShares Preferred, 2007-03), **PGX** (Invesco Preferred, 2008-01), **PGF** (Invesco Financial Preferred, 2006-12) |
| Cash leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill, 2007-05) — every Sharpe is **excess-of-cash** (minus BIL) |
| Core signal | the **(variable − fixed)** monthly total-return spread (cash cancels); flagship pair **VRP − PFF** bounded at 2014-06, multi-name sleeve at 2020-07 (PFFV) |
| Execution / costs | the regime-switch tilt uses one documented lag (rising-rate signal at month-end `t−1` → sleeve held over month `t`); the costed isolation spread charges 2 sides × one-way × NAV per rebalance + 40 bps/yr borrow on the short fixed leg |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the monthly spread; one-sample & Welch *t*; block-bootstrap (block 6, 2000 draws) CI on the spread mean and the Sharpe advantage; an era cut at 2022-01; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Short history — named on the Signal axis.** The variable-rate preferred ETFs are **young**:
VRP has ~12 years, PFFV barely six, and the entire thesis leans on a **single** high-rate episode
(the 2022 hiking cycle). One regime is not a law — the magnitudes here are one draw from one cycle.

## The headline — variable vs fixed, excess-of-cash (flagship VRP vs PFF)

Full common window 2014-06 → 2026-06 (n = **145** months):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| VRP excess-of-cash Sharpe | **+0.45** |
| PFF excess-of-cash Sharpe | **+0.23** |
| Sharpe advantage (VRP − PFF) | **+0.23** |
| (VRP − PFF) spread | **+1.28 %/yr** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* / one-sample *t* | **+1.44** / +1.01 |
| bootstrap spread 95% CI | **[−0.48, +3.07] %/yr** (includes 0) |
| bootstrap Sharpe-advantage 95% CI | **[−0.00, +0.57]** (touches 0) |

Over the **full** sample the variable sleeve out-carries the fixed one, but the edge is **thin and
not robust**: the spread's HAC *t* is only **+1.44** and a block bootstrap keeps the CI across zero.
The advantage is a real *direction* but not, on its own, a robustly significant premium.

## Era cut — the whole story is in the high-rate regime

Split at **2022-01-01** (the start of the hiking cycle):

| era | n | (var − fix) spread | NW *t* | Sharpe advantage |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| low-rate 2014-06 → 2021-12 | 91 | **−0.27 %/yr** | −0.28 | −0.03 |
| high-rate 2022-01 → 2026-06 | 54 | **+3.90 %/yr** | **+2.41** | +0.40 |

The premium is **entirely regime-contingent**: essentially *zero* when rates were pinned to the
floor (2014–2021), and strongly positive with a HAC *t* clearing 2 once rates rose. This is exactly
the reset mechanism — but it also means the effect is **not era-robust**; it is a bet on the rate
regime, not a standalone anomaly.

## The 2022 crux, in calendar years (total return)

| year | variable | fixed | cash |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2019 | +19.4% | +16.0% | +2.0% |
| 2020 | +5.4% | +7.4% | +0.4% |
| 2021 | +5.1% | +4.0% | −0.1% |
| **2022** | **−11.4%** | **−19.5%** | +1.4% |
| 2023 | +10.5% | +8.8% | +4.9% |
| 2024 | +10.3% | +6.6% | +5.2% |
| 2025 | +4.7% | +3.9% | +4.1% |

2022 is the whole case: the fixed sleeve lost **−19.5%** as rates ripped higher; the variable sleeve
reset its coupons and lost only **−11.4%**. In the low-rate years the two are a coin-flip.

## Equity-like drawdowns — the yield is not free

Preferreds are junior, equity-like credit. Full-history max-drawdowns (total return):

| sleeve | ann. return | vol | max drawdown | excess Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| variable (VRP,PFFV) | +4.88% | 7.7% | **−16.7%** | +0.40 |
| fixed (PFF,PGX,PGF) | +4.46% | 15.8% | **−59.4%** (2008–09) | +0.19 |
| VRP | +5.19% | 7.5% | −16.7% | +0.45 |
| PFF | +4.87% | 15.5% | −56.6% (2008–09) | +0.22 |

The fixed sleeve fell **~57–59%** in the GFC — a genuinely equity-like tail. The variable sleeve is
younger (post-2014) so its worst is the −16.7% of the 2020/2022 stress; over its life its carry
*does* survive its (milder) drawdowns, excess Sharpe +0.40.

## Multi-name sleeve (adds PFFV from 2020-07)

Variable (VRP, PFFV) vs fixed (PFF, PGX, PGF), 2020-07 → 2026-06 (n = **73**):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| variable excess Sharpe | +0.39 |
| fixed excess Sharpe | −0.04 |
| Sharpe advantage | **+0.43** |
| spread | **+3.21 %/yr** (NW *t* = **+2.49**) |

On the young PFFV-inclusive window the advantage clears the bar too — but this window is *all*
high-rate regime, so it is the same 2022+ story, not independent evidence.

## Tradability — the spread is real-but-thin, timing it doesn't help

**Costed isolation spread** (long variable / short fixed, dollar-neutral; 2 sides × one-way × NAV
per rebalance + 40 bps/yr borrow), full window:

| one-way cost | gross | charge | net | net NW *t* | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 4 bps | +1.28%/yr | 0.48% | **+0.80 %/yr** | +0.90 | +0.18 |
| 8 bps | +1.28%/yr | 0.56% | **+0.72 %/yr** | +0.81 | +0.16 |

**Regime-switch tilt** (hold variable when the trailing-6m rising-rate signal > 0, else fixed; one
lag; n = 145, 60 switches, 55% in variable):

| book | net excess Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| regime switch | +0.26 (+3.84 %/yr) |
| always-fixed | +0.21 |
| **always-variable** | **+0.40** |

Two honest findings. (1) The long-short isolation nets only **+0.72–0.80 %/yr** (Sharpe ~0.17,
*t* < 1) over the full sample — too thin to bank as a market-neutral spread. (2) **Timing adds
nothing**: the naive always-hold-variable book (excess Sharpe +0.40) beats the rising-rate switch
(+0.26); the switch just churns costs. The bankable read is *tilt structurally toward variable-rate
preferreds and hold*, not trade the regime.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded monthly world: a common credit factor drives both sleeves; in the high-rate
regime the fixed sleeve eats a duration hit while the variable sleeve resets and earns a planted
edge. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* | high-regime spread | low-regime spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| planted (edge = 0.30%/mo, seed 909) | **+3.11** | +17.67 %/yr | −1.10 %/yr |
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.07** (sd 1.10), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** | — | — |

The detector recovers a *planted*, regime-contingent reset premium cleanly and stays silent on the
null (1/20 ≈ the 5% false-positive rate). *(A faithful-engine check only — never cited in support of
the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The reset premium is **real but entirely regime-contingent**. Over the full
  2014–2026 tape the variable-minus-fixed spread is a thin **+1.28 %/yr** with HAC *t* = **+1.44** and
  a bootstrap CI across zero — not robust. Split by regime it *flips on*: **−0.27 %/yr** (*t* = −0.28)
  when rates were floored, **+3.90 %/yr** (*t* = **+2.41**) in the 2022+ high-rate regime, where the
  variable sleeve lost 8 points less than the fixed one in 2022. It is a genuine mechanical effect in
  the high-rate regime, but it does **not** hold across sub-eras, so it is Mixed, not Real. *Short
  history: one hiking cycle of evidence — named on the Signal axis.*
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The market-neutral long-variable / short-fixed isolation nets only
  **+0.72 %/yr** (Sharpe +0.16, *t* < 1) after costs — too thin to bank as a spread — and timing the
  regime (switch Sharpe +0.26) *underperforms* simply holding variable (+0.40). The honest, bankable
  form is a **structural tilt toward variable-rate preferreds**, whose positive carry does survive its
  milder drawdowns net of buy-and-hold costs; but the *edge over fixed* is thin, regime-dependent and
  rests on a single cycle. Real-but-thin → **Fragile**, not Investable.
